text: This is one film, made from one library. Every frame you are about to see is a motion you can reuse.
616 motions. 97 transitions. 148 styles. All built to connect.
Titles and kinetic type come first. Every word is a prop, so your copy, fonts and colours drop straight in.
Backdrops set the world. Mountains, oceans and night skies loop seamlessly, so they also work behind a website hero.
Particles and effects add life on top. They render on transparent backgrounds, so they layer over anything.
Characters and mascots wave, think and react, and they say whatever lines you give them.
Charts take plain JSON data. Bar races, donut charts and waterfalls animate themselves, in your own brand colours.
Diagrams too: flows, networks and organisation charts, drawn from a simple list of nodes and links.
Annotation overlays point at what matters: steps, clicks, arrows and call-outs, on top of your own screen recordings.
Interface loops show a product working: glass cards, chats, toasts and success states, ready for landing pages.
For social and marketing there are milestones, reviews and testimonials, in sixteen by nine, square and vertical.
E-commerce runs the whole journey: browse, add to cart, grab the deal, and the order is confirmed.
Product shots get callouts, colourways, exploded views and price tags, around your own product photo.
Documents can zoom to the line that matters, then seal it with a certificate or print the receipt.
Maps draw routes, flight arcs and city labels from real coordinates.
Camera moves add the language of film: dolly zooms, whip pans, rack focus and crash zooms, on any image.
Textures are the finishing pass: light leaks, bokeh, grain and letterbox, over any shot or photo.
For music there are now playing cards, beat-synced rings and equalisers, vinyl, and lyric videos.
Gaming and esports get versus splashes, level ups and achievements, over gameplay or pixel worlds.
Sports get kick-off countdowns, line-ups, live match stats and podiums.
News and documentary get breaking banners, name supers and fact checks.
For lessons and kids there are quizzes, counting games and equations that solve themselves.
Events and celebrations get countdowns, fireworks and tickets for the big night.
Every video needs a front door and an exit: logo reveals, stings and end screens.
Presentation slides animate too: big numbers, feature columns and agendas, with alpha for Keynote and PowerPoint.
Developer and AI explainers show code diffs, build pipelines and streaming chat.
And when you need depth, real 3D renders live: terrain fly-overs, islands, rooms that build themselves, and spinning type.
The style engine restyles any of it with one word. Here is one shot, as a blueprint, a screen-printed poster, and eight-bit pixels.
And 97 transitions stitch it all together.
In a Remotion project, mgl add copies only the motions you choose into your own source.
On React and Next.js sites, MotionBackground puts a live motion behind your real HTML, and it pauses off screen.
On any HTML page or WordPress site, it is one script tag and an opus motion element.
Video editors and apps get exported files with alpha, or call the HTTP render API.
And AI agents can search, preview and render every motion themselves, through the built in MCP server.
That is the whole library. Every one of the 616 motions, all connected.
Opus Motion is free and open source. Find it on GitHub, and if it helps you make something, leave a star.
